response.sql: WITH per_tif AS (SELECT o.timespan AS time_in_force, COUNT(DISTINCT o.recordvault) AS order_count FROM orders o JOIN riskandmargin r ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault GROUP BY o.timespan), shares AS (SELECT time_in_force, order_count, order_count * 1.0 / SUM(order_count) OVER () AS share FROM per_tif) SELECT time_in_force, order_count, share, share - AVG(share) OVER () AS diff_from_avg_share FROM shares ORDER BY time_in_force

assumptions.assumption: Orders are identified by recordvault (the unique order reference); orders.orderspivot is a different key but one-to-one with it, so distinct counts are the same.

Share is a fraction of 1 (not a percentage), and the difference is share minus the simple (unweighted) average of shares across the time-in-force values present after the join; time-in-force values with no matched risk/margin records do not appear and are not part of the average.
Orders with a NULL timespan, if any, form their own group (NULL time in force) and are included in the total and the average.

alternatives.interpretation: Exclude orders with a NULL timespan, so the total and average are over actual time-in-force values only.
alternatives.sql: WITH per_tif AS (SELECT o.timespan AS time_in_force, COUNT(DISTINCT o.recordvault) AS order_count FROM orders o JOIN riskandmargin r ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault WHERE o.timespan IS NOT NULL GROUP BY o.timespan), shares AS (SELECT time_in_force, order_count, order_count * 1.0 / SUM(order_count) OVER () AS share FROM per_tif) SELECT time_in_force, order_count, share, share - AVG(share) OVER () AS diff_from_avg_share FROM shares ORDER BY time_in_force
